text:
ashley: quick check — thinking about our internal API shape for user-routing/quotas and console UX. Do we standardize on gRPC/protos everywhere, or keep HTTP/JSON at the edge and translate? Concerns: per-route quotas, per-model routing, telemetry labels, and rollout canaries. Thoughts?

matt: leaning gRPC for backend services. typed contracts + proto options make client SDKs safer. telemetry easier if we inject labels server-side. but browser clients -> need a gateway.

priya: +1 to gateway for browser. For telemetry/quotas we need a single place that emits consistent route labels anyway. gateway-transcode can do that.

ben: caveat: transcoding hides semantics. edge JSON -> backend proto mismatch causes weird 400s. Also harder to reason about partial rollouts if we have multiple gateways.

kate: UX ask from console: we want per-route latency/cost breakdowns tied to model_version and route_claims. That requires headers or trace attrs to survive the gateway->service hop. how do we propagate? example header idea:

```
X-Route-Name: generate_text
X-Model-Version: gptx-4-quant
X-Tenant-ID: t_acme
```

We should standardize header names and map them to spans.

infra-bot: suggested config snippet for envoy header passthrough:

```
- name: envoy.filters.http.router
  typed_config: {}
  request_headers_to_add:
    - header: { key: 'x-route-name', value: '%REQ(X-ROUTE-NAME)%' }
```

matt: another option: keep proto-first for service-to-service. expose a small HTTP JSON facade at the edge that normalizes payloads and emits route labels. that facade can also handle auth/quotas. minimizes client footprint.

priya: important: quotas need to be charged at the enforcement point. If we do only edge enforcement, what about platform-internal consumers? We'll need an enforcer library or token that the services trust.

ashley: good point. for dedicated capacity clients (internal batch jobs) we'd prefer direct gRPC to avoid gateway hops and cost. but then we lose unified quota enforcement unless services call a central charge API.

ben: implementation pattern: services call QuotaService v1 via gRPC (a single RPC per request or batched). QuotaService enforces and returns tokens. lightweight and consistent.

sam: can we avoid double-counting? e.g., gateway charges then backend charges again. we should document an idempotent charge flow: gateway attaches `X-Quota-Token` and backend validates no extra charge.

kate: rollout UX: console needs to show canary split and fallback. If we do proto-first, rollouts are per-model server side. If we do gateway routing, we can do traffic-splitting at the edge and preserve metrics. Edge-based split is easier for canaries.

deploy-bot: canary deployed edge-facade v0.3 -> 10% traffic -> :white_check_mark:

ashley: thanks. Action items: (1) prototype edge facade that emits standardized headers + quota tokens (sam+priya) (2) QuotaService proto design (ben + matt) (3) doc w/ header specs + console mapping (kate). I'll create RFC template.

sam: happy to prototype, will spin up a lightweight node proxy that does proto->json transcode + header enrichment. ping me for infra creds.

matt: +1. let's also add a telemetry test that asserts labels are present end-to-end (edge -> trace -> console ingestion).

ashley: perfect. I'll open an RFC and link the prototype PR once ready. :thumbsup:
